title: Forms of Government
text: Common forms of government include democracy (rule by the people, directly or through elected representatives), monarchy (rule by a king/queen), and republic (a state without a hereditary ruler, typically with elected leadership).

title: Features of Democracy
text: Key features of democracy typically include free and fair elections, rule of law, protection of fundamental rights, separation of powers, and government accountability to citizens.

title: Role of Political Parties
text: Political parties organize citizens around shared policy positions, field candidates for election, and form or oppose governments, helping structure political competition and representation.

title: Pressure Groups
text: Pressure groups (interest groups) are organizations that seek to influence government policy on specific issues without themselves seeking to win elections and govern directly, unlike political parties.

title: Federal vs Unitary Government
text: In a federal system, power is constitutionally divided between a central government and regional/state governments. In a unitary system, like The Gambia's, power is concentrated in the central government, which may delegate some authority to local government.
